correctness.rationale: The integral H(e^t-1) expansion is coefficientwise finite, and m!S(n,m) permits a FINITE power-sum truncation for each modulus because sufficiently large factorials vanish modulo 2^r. The directly reconstructed a(6)=1431665 and a(8)=6646603073 imply the decisive odd-square coefficient B=2 mod 4. For odd j, j²=1+8beta_j; binomial valuations give the claimed 2^(r-3) period, and the difference at half that period is exactly 2^(r-1) mod 2^r at every large even n, excluding all proper divisors. Parity and mod 4/8 supply small cases. I independently computed ten EGF coefficients by odd-subset sums and checked small exact dyadic increment cases; these finite tests do not establish the infinite quantifiers.
